title: Ids that two branches cannot both mint
description: F471, operator decision option (c): branch-suffix ids for bugs, phases and tasks, plus a resolve verb for the collisions that remain.
desiredOutcome: Two branches that each add a bug, a phase and a task allocate different ids and merge with the driver with no conflict; a collision that still happens (both on the development branch) is resolved by one verb that renumbers the named side and every reference to it.

tasks.title: The id shape, named once: branch suffix, numeric part, the widened patterns
tasks.description: E1a: _id_shape (suffix from branch, trunk set from _branch.parent_branch, numeric part) and the BUG/DEC/PROP patterns widened additively in vocab and schema.

outcome.technical: _id_shape: trunk set via _branch.parent_branch plus origin/HEAD, no suffix without a trunk, base36 of sha1(branch); BUG/PROP patterns widened from _manifest_vocab.ID_SUFFIX.
outcome.descriptive: Ids minted off the development branch carry a branch suffix, so two branches cannot mint the same bug, task or proposal id; the development branch keeps today's ids.

tasks.title: Allocators and id readers speak the branch-suffix shape
tasks.description: E1b+E2: task and phase allocation through _id_shape with the current branch's suffix; a next-id bug verb; the prefix warning, the usage task-id regex, the bug finding text and the bug renumberer read suffixed ids.

outcome.technical: audit-task add via _id_shape; next-id bug|prop (--json); prefix warning, findings, renumberer and usage attribution read suffixed ids.
outcome.descriptive: Task ids, and the bug and proposal ids the model writes by hand, come from one allocator that knows the branch; every reader of the old shape reads the new one.

tasks.title: A phase on a side branch is warned once and can be parked as a proposal instead
tasks.description: Operator decision: phases are minted on the development branch. add-phase on a side branch still writes (never blocked) but warns the first time on that branch, read from the phase.add rows that now carry the branch; add-phase --park writes the same phase as a proposal (PROP-<n>-<suffix>) to materialize after the phase branch merges.

outcome.technical: add-phase --park via _park_phase; side-branch warning read from phase.add rows carrying branch (DETAILS_KEYS); _journal_cfg shared by write and read.
outcome.descriptive: A phase added on a phase branch is never blocked; the first one on a branch is warned, and --park defers it as a proposal to materialize after the merge.

tasks.title: README and CHANGELOG say where phases are minted and what --park and next-id do
tasks.description: The README command-table row the cf1 lint reads, and the Unreleased section, for P61.1-P61.3.

outcome.descriptive: The README and CHANGELOG state where phases are minted and what --park and next-id do.

tasks.title: close-phase offers materialize for proposals parked on the merged branch
tasks.description: Once a phase branch merges, the proposals parked on it are listed with the materialize command for the parent branch; the proposal step is not left to memory.

outcome.technical: _proposals.parked_on_branch read from the landed copy inside close-phase's stamp step; rendered with the materialize commands.
outcome.descriptive: When a phase branch lands, sign-off lists the proposals it parked and the command to materialize each on the parent.

tasks.title: Real-git proof that sign-off names the proposals a merged branch parked
tasks.description: g16b: a phase branch in a worktree parks a proposal, close-phase lands it, and the output names the proposal and the materialize command for the parent.

outcome.descriptive: A real merge proves the parked proposals are named after landing.

tasks.title: One reference renamer: an id renamed everywhere the plan points at it
tasks.description: rename(manifest, mapping) rewrites the id and every field that holds it - blockedBy, dependsOn, bugId, taskId, fileIndex, proposal payloads, materializedAs - and never movedFrom, which is history. renumber_duplicate_bugs uses it instead of its two-field rewrite.

outcome.technical: _id_refs.rename/phase_mapping/collisions over the schema's id-holding fields; movedFrom untouched.
outcome.descriptive: Renaming an id rewrites every reference to it in one place, so no reference can be left pointing at an id that no longer exists.

tasks.title: A proposal parked on a side branch reserves a placeholder the development branch mints for real
tasks.description: Found by probe: two branches each parking a proposal both reserve P<max+1>, and the merged plan carries a finding neither side had, so the driver leaves the merge conflicted. A side-branch park reserves P<n>-<suffix>; materialize re-mints it as the next P<n> and renames it and every reference through _id_refs; branch is a known proposal key.

outcome.technical: placeholder P<n>-<suffix> at park; plan_for re-mints by the append rule; apply_materialize renames across the plan via _id_refs; branch known in vocab and schema.
outcome.descriptive: Two phase branches that each park new work now merge cleanly; the development branch gives each parked phase its real id when it is materialized, and every reference follows.

tasks.title: The demo fixture carries proposal.branch, and its rendered artifacts follow
tasks.description: The schema gained proposal.branch; the demo fixture must carry every schema field, and every artifact rendered from it is re-derived.

outcome.descriptive: The demo carries the new field; no rendered page changes.

tasks.title: With several phases running, a task added without --phase goes to the phase whose branch is checked out
tasks.description: Three developers leave several in_progress phases in the index; 'the current phase' is the one whose recorded branch is checked out, not whichever one is in_progress. No match keeps the --phase requirement.

outcome.technical: _resolve_phase matches phase.branch to the checked-out branch; basis returned, printed or carried as phaseBasis.
outcome.descriptive: With several phases running, a task added without --phase lands in the phase whose branch is checked out.

tasks.title: merge-manifest resolve: renumber the side the operator names, every reference with it
tasks.description: For the collision the suffix cannot prevent - two clones minting on the development branch - resolve reads the conflicted file's three stages, renames each id both sides added on the side the operator names to the next free id (with every reference, via _id_refs), re-merges and validates; in the sharded layout a colliding phase's shard is written under its new name. The driver's conflict message names the verb.

outcome.technical: merge-manifest resolve: three plans from HEAD/MERGE_HEAD/base via git archive + load_manifest, _id_refs rename on the named side, re-merge, sharded write via split_manifest; build_parser for the non-driver verbs.
outcome.descriptive: A bug, task, proposal or phase id minted on both sides of a merge on the development branch is resolved by one command that renumbers the side the user names, with every reference.

tasks.title: split_manifest keeps every root key, so a sharded save cannot drop decisions (F469)
tasks.description: split_manifest copied four named root keys, so decisions and every unknown root key vanished on /audit:layout sharded and every save_sharded caller - breaking COMPATIBILITY's tolerated-unknown-keys promise. resolve is about to save through it too.

outcome.technical: split_manifest copies every root key; the four known ones first, in their old order.
outcome.descriptive: A sharded save no longer drops decisions or any root key a later release adds.

tasks.title: next-id task --phase: the id a hand-written fix or moved task takes
tasks.description: /audit:bug fix and /audit:task move write a task by hand and computed <phaseId>.<next> themselves - max+1, on whatever branch, with no suffix. next-id task --phase <id> prints the allocator's answer, reservations and suffix included.

outcome.technical: next-id task --phase via _allocate_id with the branch suffix.
outcome.descriptive: A fix task or a moved task written by hand takes its id from the same allocator as every other task.

tasks.title: The commands stop computing max+1 by hand and say where phases are minted
tasks.description: Every prose step that allocated BUG-, PROP- or <phaseId>.<n> by hand calls next-id; bug fix prefers the current phase and never mints a BF phase on a phase branch; init and sync pull stop on a phase branch; manifest-conventions states the suffix, the placeholder and resolve; worktree.md's promise is scoped (F470); COMPATIBILITY names the forward-compat cost.
